Main.sentence: Hezbollah [a] is a ___E:Lebanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_people)___ ___E:Shia Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islamism)___ political party and ___E:paramilitary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramilitary)___ group.

Hezbollah's paramilitary wing is the ___E:Jihad Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jihad_Council)___ ,  and its political wing is the ___E:Loyalty to the Resistance Bloc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loyalty_to_the_Resistance_Bloc)___ party in the ___E:Lebanese Parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Lebanon)___ . ___E:Its armed strength U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hezbollah_armed_strength)___ was assessed to be equivalent to that of a medium-sized army in 2016.
Hezbollah was founded in 1982 by Lebanese clerics in response to the ___E:Israeli invasion of Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Lebanon_War)___ .

Inspired by the ___E:Iranian Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_Revolution)___ of 1979 and Ayatollah ___E:Ruhollah Khomeini U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruhollah_Khomeini)___ 's model of Islamic governance, Hezbollah established strong ties with Iran. The group was initially supported by 1,500 ___E:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Revolutionary_Guard_Corps)___ (IRGC) instructors, who helped unify various Lebanese Shia factions under Hezbollah's leadership.

Hezbollah's 1985 manifesto outlined ___E:its key objectives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ideology_of_Hezbollah)___ , which include expelling Western influence from the region, ___E:destroying Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calls_for_the_destruction_of_Israel)___ , pledging allegiance to ___E:Iran's supreme leader U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Leader_of_Iran)___ , and establishing an ___E:Islamic government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_republic)___ influenced by ___E:Iran's political ideology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khomeinism)___ .
However, the manifesto also emphasized Lebanese self-determination.

Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, Hezbollah fought against Israeli forces and the ___E:South Lebanon Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Lebanon_Army)___ (SLA), eventually leading to Israel's withdrawal from southern Lebanon in 2000.  Hezbollah also played a prominent role in the ___E:2006 Lebanon War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Lebanon_War)___ and later became involved in the ___E:Syrian civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_civil_war)___ , where it fought alongside the Syrian government against rebel forces.
In 2009, Hezbollah updated their manifesto to oppose political sectarianism, appeal to non-Islamic movements, and promote a national unity government.
The updated manifesto has the same basic approach to foreign policy, emphasizing the hegemonic strategies of the US and Israel's role in the region as a forward base for colonizing the region.
Since the 1990s, Hezbollah has grown into a significant political force in Lebanon.
The group operates a vast social services network, including schools and hospitals, and runs a satellite TV station, ___E:Al-Manar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Manar)___ .
Politically, Hezbollah's Loyalty to the Resistance Bloc holds 15 seats in the Lebanese Parliament, making it a powerful player in Lebanon's government.
However, the group's influence has led to growing domestic criticism.

Following the ___E:2020 Beirut port explosion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Beirut_explosion)___ , Hezbollah was accused of obstructing efforts to hold those responsible accountable, contributing to a decline in public trust.
A 2024 Arab Barometer survey found that 55% of Lebanese have "no trust at all" in Hezbollah, although it remains popular among the Shia population.

Despite calls for disarmament under ___E:United Nations Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council)___ resolutions, Hezbollah has expanded its military capabilities.

Its armed wing is now considered stronger than the ___E:Lebanese Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_Armed_Forces)___ ,  making it one of the most powerful non-state actors in the world.
Hezbollah leader ___E:Hassan Nasrallah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hassan_Nasrallah)___ declared in 2021 that the group had 100,000 fighters.

Hezbollah has been involved in several high-profile attacks; it is believed to be responsible for the ___E:bombing of the US embassy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_US_embassy_bombing_in_Beirut)___ and the ___E:American and French barracks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Beirut_barracks_bombings)___ bombings in Beirut in 1983, the ___E:assassination of Rafic Hariri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Rafic_Hariri)___ in 2005,   as well as later attacks, including bombings and hijackings.

While Hezbollah has been regarded as a ___E:resistance movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resistance_movement)___ by some scholars,    the entire organization, or its military wing alone, has been designated as a ___E:terrorist group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_designated_terrorist_groups)___  by at least 27 countries, as of October 2020, including most Western countries.
Since October 2023, Hezbollah has been ___E:at war with Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Hezbollah_conflict_(2023%E2%80%93present))___ .

During this war, Nasrallah ___E:was assassinated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Hezbollah_headquarters_strike)___ after 32 years of leading the group, along with other key members of Hezbollah leadership.

The conflict has led to ___E:an Israeli invasion of Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Israeli_invasion_of_Lebanon)___ , and is currently ___E:in a ceasefire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Israel%E2%80%93Lebanon_ceasefire_agreement)___ .

On August 7, 2025 in a government meeting specifically addressing the ___E:disarmament of Hezbollah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disarmament_of_Hezbollah)___ , the majority of the government voted to approve the decision.
The Lebanese Army was tasked to create a plan ensuring that only the state has control over weapons in Lebanon.
The decision is based on a U.S. plan to disarm Hezbollah.

On September 5, the Lebanese cabinet approved the ___E:Homeland Shield Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeland_Shield_Plan)___ , the LAF's roadmap for the disarmament of all militias in Lebanon and specifically Hezbollah.

In 1982, Hezbollah was conceived by Muslim clerics and funded by ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ primarily to fight the ___E:Israeli invasion of Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Lebanon_War)___ .

The 1982 and the ___E:1978 Israeli invasions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978_South_Lebanon_conflict)___ had created a humanitarian crisis in Lebanon; many villages in the south had been destroyed and large numbers of Shias had been displaced from their homes.
In addition, the Shia had long been underrepresented in Lebanese politics.
Both these factors fostered resentment among the local Shia population, making them a fertile ground for recruitment.
Hezbollah was set up by local Shia committees, under the leadership of ___E:Ruhollah Khomeini U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruhollah_Khomeini)___ .

Its forces were trained and organized by a contingent of 1,500 ___E:Iranian Revolutionary Guards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Revolutionary_Guard_Corps)___ that arrived from Iran with permission from the ___E:Syrian government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba%27athist_Syria)___ , which ___E:occupied Lebanon's eastern highlands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_occupation_of_Lebanon)___ , permitted their transit to a base in the ___E:Bekaa valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bekaa_valley)___  which was in ___E:occupation of Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_occupation_of_Lebanon)___ at the time.
Scholars differ as to when Hezbollah came to be a distinct entity.

Various sources list the official formation of the group as early as 1982    whereas Diaz and Newman maintain that Hezbollah remained an amalgamation of various violent Shi'a extremists until as late as 1985.  Another version states that it was formed by supporters of Sheikh ___E:Ragheb Harb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragheb_Harb)___ , a leader of the southern Shia resistance killed by Israel in 1984.  Regardless of when the name came into official use, a number of Shi'a groups were slowly assimilated into the organization, such as ___E:Islamic Jihad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Jihad_Organization)___ , ___E:Organization of the Oppressed on Earth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_of_the_Oppressed_on_Earth)___ and the ___E:Revolutionary Justice Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Justice_Organization)___ .
These designations are considered to be synonymous with Hezbollah by the US,  Israel  and Canada.

According to ___E:Robert Fisk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fisk)___  and Israeli General Shimon Shapira  the date of 8 June 1982, two days after the Israeli invasion of Lebanon, when 50 ___E:Shiite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam)___ militants ambushed an ___E:Israel Defense Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces)___ armored convoy in ___E:Khalde U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalde)___ south of Beirut, is considered by Hezbollah as the founding myth of their ___E:military wing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hezbollah_armed_strength)___ .

It was in this battle, delaying the Israeli advance to Beirut for six days, that the future Hezbollah military chief ___E:Mustafa Badreddine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafa_Badreddine)___ made his name as a serious commander.

According to Shapira, the lightly armed Shia fighters managed to capture an Israeli armored vehicle on that day and paraded it in the Revolutionary Guards' ___E:forward operating base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_operating_base)___ in ___E:Baalbek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baalbek)___ , Eastern Lebanon.
Fisk writes:
Down at Khalde, a remarkable phenomenon had taken shape.

The Shia militiamen were running on foot into the Israeli gunfire to launch grenades at the Israeli armour, actually moving to within 20 feet of the tanks to open fire at them. Some of the Shia fighters had torn off pieces of their shirts and wrapped them around their heads as bands of martyrdom as the ___E:Iranian revolutionary guards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IRGC)___ had begun doing a year before when they staged their first mass attacks against the ___E:Iraqis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Army)___ in the ___E:Gulf War a thousand miles to the east U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran-Iraq_War)___ .
When they set fire to one Israeli armoured vehicle, the gunmen were emboldened to advance further.
None of us, I think, realised the critical importance of the events of Khalde that night.
The Lebanese Shia were learning the principles of martyrdom and putting them into practice.

Never before had we seen these men wear headbands like this; we thought it was another militia affectation but it was not. It was the beginning of a legend which also contained a strong element of truth.
The Shia were now the Lebanese resistance, nationalist no doubt but also inspired by their religion.
The party of God – in Arabic, the Hezbollah – were on the beaches of Khalde that night.

Hezbollah emerged in ___E:South Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Lebanon)___ during a consolidation of ___E:Shia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islam_in_Lebanon)___ militias as a rival to the older ___E:Amal Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amal_Movement)___ .

Hezbollah played a significant role in the Lebanese civil war, opposing ___E:American forces in 1982–83 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_Force_in_Lebanon)___ and opposing Amal and ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ during the 1985–88 ___E:War of the Camps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Camps)___ .
However, Hezbollah's early primary focus was ending Israel's occupation of southern Lebanon  following Israel's 1982 invasion and siege of Beirut.
Amal, the main Lebanese Shia political group, initiated ___E:guerrilla warfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerrilla_warfare)___ .
In 2006, former Israeli prime minister ___E:Ehud Barak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Barak)___ stated, "When we entered Lebanon ... there was no Hezbollah.
We were accepted with perfumed rice and flowers by the Shia in the south.
It was our presence there that created Hezbollah."

Hezbollah waged an ___E:asymmetric war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asymmetric_war)___ using ___E:suicide attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istishhad)___ against the ___E:Israel Defense Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces)___ (IDF) and Israeli targets outside of Lebanon.

Hezbollah is reputed to have been among the first Islamic resistance groups in the Middle East to use the tactics of suicide bombing, assassination, and capturing foreign soldiers,  as well as murders  and hijackings.
Hezbollah also employed more conventional military tactics and weaponry, notably ___E:Katyusha rockets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katyusha_rocket_launcher)___ and other missiles.

At the end of the Lebanese Civil War in 1990, despite the ___E:Taif Agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taif_Agreement)___ asking for the "disbanding of all Lebanese and non-Lebanese militias", ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ , which controlled Lebanon at that time, allowed Hezbollah to maintain their arsenal and control Shia areas along the border with Israel.
In the 1990s, Hezbollah transformed from a revolutionary group into a political one, in a process which has been described as the "Lebanonization" of Hezbollah.
Unlike its uncompromising revolutionary stance in the 1980s, Hezbollah conveyed a lenient stance towards the Lebanese state.

In 1992, Hezbollah decided to participate in elections, and ___E:Ali Khamenei U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Khamenei)___ , ___E:supreme leader of Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Leader_of_Iran)___ , endorsed it. Former Hezbollah secretary general, ___E:Subhi al-Tufayli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhi_al-Tufayli)___ , contested this decision, which led to a schism in Hezbollah.
Hezbollah won all twelve seats which were on its electoral list. At the end of that year, Hezbollah began to engage in dialog with Lebanese Christians.
Hezbollah regards cultural, political, and religious freedoms in Lebanon as sanctified, although it does not extend these values to groups who have relations with Israel.

In 1997, Hezbollah formed the multi-confessional ___E:Lebanese Brigades to Fight the Israeli Occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_Resistance_Brigades)___ in an attempt to revive national and secular resistance against Israel, thereby marking the "Lebanonization" of resistance.
Whether the ___E:Islamic Jihad Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Jihad_Organization)___ (IJO) was a nom de guerre used by Hezbollah or a separate organization, is disputed.
According to certain sources, IJO was identified as merely a "telephone organization",   and whose name was "used by those involved to disguise their true identity".
Hezbollah reportedly also used another name, "Islamic Resistance" ( al-Muqawama al-Islamiyya ), for attacks against Israel.  : 67
A 2003 American court decision found IJO was the name used by Hezbollah for its attacks in Lebanon, parts of the Middle East and Europe.
The US,  Israel  and Canada  consider the names "Islamic Jihad Organization", "Organization of the Oppressed on Earth" and the "Revolutionary Justice Organization" to be synonymous with Hezbollah.

The group receives substantial financial and military backing from ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ , by ___E:smuggling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_smuggling_to_Lebanon)___ and other measures,    positioning itself as the leading member of the " ___E:Axis of Resistance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_of_Resistance)___ ", an alliance in opposition to ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ and ___E:Western influence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westernization)___ in the Middle East.  Following the outcome of the ___E:Israeli invasion of Lebanon (2024–present) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Israeli_invasion_of_Lebanon)___ , the ___E:2024 Syrian opposition offensives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Syrian_opposition_offensives)___ , the ___E:downfall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Assad_regime)___ of the ___E:Assad regime U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba%27athist_Syria)___ and the weakening of the ___E:Axis of Resistance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_of_Resistance)___ , Hezbollah has withdrawn the majority of its military infrastructure from southern Lebanon, transferring control to the Lebanese army.     This move aligns with the November 2024 U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement, which mandates Hezbollah's repositioning north of the Litani River and the deployment of approximately 5,000 Lebanese troops to the south.
The withdrawal aims to reduce tensions along the Israel-Lebanon border and facilitate the return of displaced civilians.

While Hezbollah has removed heavy weaponry, some fighters from southern villages remain with light arms. The situation remains delicate, with ongoing monitoring by international observers to ensure compliance with the ceasefire terms,   although Israel has violated the ceasefire terms in near-daily basis.

As part of the ceasefire agreement that ended the ___E:2024 Israeli invasion of Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Israeli_invasion_of_Lebanon)___ , and with mounting pressure from the US, the Lebanese Armed Forces have undertaken efforts to disarm Hezbollah, including in its traditional strongholds in southern Lebanon, with the aid of Israeli intelligence.

In May 2025, the Lebanese government had announced that the army had largely achieved its aim.   On 5 August 2025, the ___E:Lebanese government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanese_government)___ declared that a plan would be scheduled for the disarmament of the militias after a six-hour cabinet meeting with president ___E:Joseph Aoun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Aoun)___ .
According to the Lebanese government, Hezbollah has handed over control of several critical facilities.
Information minister ___E:Paul Morcos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Morcos)___ stated that a deadline of the end of 2025 was set for disarmament.

Hezbollah leader ___E:Naim Qassem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naim_Qassem)___ condemned the disarmament proposal, stating: "The resistance is fine, strong and ready to fight for Lebanon's sovereignty and independence...

Hezbollah made heavy sacrifices to defend Lebanon against the Israeli aggression." He warned that Hezbollah was prepared to renew attacks on Israel and said all of Lebanon would unite to counter Israel.

On 22 August, Qassem threatened a ___E:civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_war)___ if the disarmament proposal went forward, which prime minister ___E:Nawaf Salam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawaf_Salam)___ condemned as "completely unacceptable".
On 7 August, the cabinet of ministers approved the objective of the disarmament proposal, ensuring that arms in Lebanon are only possessed by the state.

Hezbollah and ___E:Amal Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amal_Movement)___ -affiliated ministers walked out of the cabinet meeting in protest,  and thousands of Hezbollah supporters rallied against the approval in the southern suburbs of Beirut.
On 5 September, the Lebanese army presented the disarmament plan to the government.
On September 5, 2025 General Rodolphe Haykal presented to the Lebanese cabinet the Homeland Shield Plan, its roadmap for the disarmament of all militias in Lebanon, specifically Hezbollah.

The ideology of Hezbollah has been summarized as ___E:Shia Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia_Islamist)___ ___E:radicalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_radicalism)___ ;   Hezbollah follows the Islamic ___E:Shia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia)___ theology developed by Iranian leader ___E:Ayatollah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayatollah)___ Ruhollah Khomeini.

Hezbollah was largely formed with the aid of the Khomeini's followers in the early 1980s in order to spread ___E:Islamic revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_revolution)___  and follows a distinct version of Islamic Shia ideology ( ___E:Wilayat al-faqih U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hokumat-e_Islami_:_Velayat-e_faqih_(book_by_Khomeini))___ or Guardianship of the Islamic Jurists) developed by Khomeini, who was the leader of the "Islamic Revolution" in ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ .

Although Hezbollah originally aimed to transform Lebanon into an ___E:Islamic republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_republic)___ , this goal has been abandoned in favor of a more inclusive approach.
Early on, Hezbollah was influenced by ideas from prominent Sunni Islamists.
Hezbollah's own rhetoric was Islamist in general, rather than Shia in particular.

Hezbollah's position on the Sunni-Shia divide was that instead of dwelling on theological differences, Sunnis and Shias ought to cooperate with one another to oppose the Israeli occupation of Arab lands.

To maintain a sense of Muslim unity, Hezbollah avoided direct criticism of Saudi Arabia; even during the ___E:2007 Lebanon's conflict with the Salafis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Lebanon_conflict)___ , Al-Manar TV's employees had instructions "not to talk badly about Saudi Arabia".
This changed, however, after the beginning of the ___E:Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi-led_intervention_in_the_Yemeni_civil_war)___ .
Hezbollah has been described as ___E:socially conservative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_conservatism)___ .
It is ___E:against homosexuality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobia)___ and ___E:LGBT rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights_by_country_or_territory)___ .
In 2023, Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah called for gay people to be killed and said that the LGBT community was a "threat to society".

The organization also encourages women to wear traditional ___E:Islamic veils U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_veiling_practices_by_country)___ , especially the full-body ___E:chador U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chador)___ .

Some scholars consider Hezbollah to have become a left-wing political movement;  including political scientists Anisseh van Engeland and Rachael Rudolph,  ___E:Imad Salamey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imad_Salamey)___ , ___E:Amal Saad-Ghorayeb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amal_Saad-Ghorayeb)___ , and ___E:As'ad Abu Khalil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/As%27ad_AbuKhalil)___ .
Salamey described Hezbollah as "a revolutionary proletarian party with an Islamic manifesto".
Feminist ___E:Judith Butler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judith_Butler)___ controversially called Hezbollah part of the "global left" because they define themselves as anti-imperialist.

Communist writer ___E:Nahla Chahal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahla_Chahal)___ wrote that Hezhollah "is a movement of the ___E:Theology of Liberation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_theology#Palestinian_liberation_theology)___ ".
On 16 February 1985, Sheik Ibrahim al-Amin issued Hezbollah's manifesto.

The ideology presented in it was described as radical. [by whom?] Its first objective was to ___E:fight against U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-imperialism)___ what Hezbollah described as ___E:American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_imperialism)___ and ___E:Israeli imperialism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_the_West_Bank)___ , including the ___E:Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_occupation_of_Southern_Lebanon)___ and other territories.

The second objective was to gather all Muslims into an " ___E:ummah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ummah)___ ", under which Lebanon would further the aims of the ___E:1979 Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1979_Revolution)___ of Iran. It also declared it would protect all Lebanese communities, excluding those that collaborated with Israel, and support all national movements—both Muslim and non-Muslim—throughout the world. [which?]
Translated excerpts from Hezbollah's original 1985 manifesto read:
We are the sons of the umma (Muslim community) ... ...

We are an ummah linked to the Muslims of the whole world by the solid doctrinal and religious connection of Islam, whose message God wanted to be fulfilled by the Seal of the ___E:Prophets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prophets_of_Islam)___ , i.e., Prophet ___E:Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad)___ . ...

As for our culture, it is based on the Holy ___E:Quran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quran)___ , the ___E:Sunna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunnah)___ and the legal rulings of the faqih who is our source of imitation ...
On 30 November 2009, secretary-general ___E:Nasrallah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hassan_Nasrallah)___ presented a new manifesto at Hezbollah's 7th political conference.

Besides its introduction, this 32-page document has three chapters on U.S. hegemonic strategies and the impact of ___E:globalization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization)___ ; Hezbollah's approach to Lebanon; and Palestinian resistance to Israel.

While self-described as a "rebirth" document, the manifesto conveys the same basic approach to foreign policy as in the past, according to scholar ___E:Benedetta Berti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedetta_Berti)___ , though it is more "politically savvy" and appeals to non-Islamic movements.
Still, the manifesto offers new support for Lebanese political institutions, through which it had been making inroads.
Notably, it says that it opposes political "sectarianism", idealizes a national unity government, and treats the Lebanese army less as an enemy and more as a subordinate military arm.

From the inception of Hezbollah to the present,   ___E:the elimination of the State of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calls_for_the_destruction_of_Israel)___ has been one of Hezbollah's primary goals.
Some translations of Hezbollah's 1985 Arabic-language manifesto state that "our struggle will end only when this entity [Israel] is obliterated".

According to Hezbollah's Deputy-General, ___E:Naim Qassem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naim_Qassem)___ , the struggle against Israel is a core belief of Hezbollah and the central rationale of Hezbollah's existence.

Hezbollah says that its continued hostilities against Israel are justified as reciprocal to Israeli operations against Lebanon and as retaliation for what they claim is Israel's occupation of Lebanese territory.

Israel withdrew from Lebanon in 2000, and their withdrawal was verified by the United Nations as being in accordance with resolution 425 of 19 March 1978; however, Lebanon considers the ___E:Shebaa farms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shebaa_farms)___ —a 26 km 2 (10 sq mi) piece of land captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 war and considered by the UN to be Syrian territory occupied by Israel—to be Lebanese territory.
Finally, Hezbollah considers Israel to be an illegitimate state.
For these reasons, it justifies its actions as acts of defensive jihad.
If they go from Shebaa, we won't stop fighting them. ...
Our goal is to liberate the 1948 borders of Palestine, ...

The Jews who survive this war of liberation can ___E:go back to Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_back_to_Poland)___ or wherever they came from. However, that the Jews who lived in Palestine before 1948 will be 'allowed to live as a minority and they will be cared for by the Muslim majority.'
Hezbollah officials have said, on rare occasions, that it is only "anti-Zionist" and not anti-Semitic.
